newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's INA, Agip to expand gas project.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's INA, Agip to expand gas project.

text.p: Croatia's state oil company INA and Italy's Agip SpA will sign a contract late in June to expand their joint exploration of natural gas in the Adriatic, an official at INA said.
According to a letter of intent, INA and Agip will explore 2,500 square km of the central Adriatic in addition to 1,860 square km already searched in the north.
Agip will fully cover the cost of exploring the new field named Aiza-Laura, put at $24 million, and provide technology and equipment, neccessary for three-dimensional seismic analysis.

"Exploration is the riskiest phase, but by the logic of geological similarity with the Italian side, this field has good potential," INA's director of research and exploration, Marijan Pejcic, told Reuters.
Agip operates some 100 offshore platforms in the Adriatic.

The estimates of offshore gas reserves in the four northern fields were put at 12 billion standard cubic metres (scm) and the two firms recently agreed to build an offshore platform for gas exploration.
INA and Agip, which previously cooperated in third countries including Egypt and Angola, have already spent $40 million in the Adriatic gas project launched two years ago.
"If all is well the first research will start in the autumn," Pejcic said.

He said that after the research phase, the companies would take an equal share of the profits. The Italian side will be compensated for paying the research costs by taking surplus gas over a period of time.
Futher plans include a pipeline to link Ravenna in Italy with Pula nad Rijeka on the Croatian coast. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Nesroom, 385-1-4557075
